name: CSC VLE TOOLS - upload to GitHub with VS Code
which_zip_to_upload: CSC_VLE_TOOLS_v31.zip (full version). Do NOT upload the standalone zip.

steps.title: Unzip the new version into a simple folder
do: Right-click CSC_VLE_TOOLS_v31.zip (or the newest zip) and choose Extract All. Extract to C:\csc-v31. Use a short folder name with NO # or & signs, because PowerShell cannot read them.
Open the folder: index.html, assets and many tools_*.html files must be directly inside.
Upload ONLY the full version. The standalone zip is only for testing one tool at a time.

steps.title: Clone your real GitHub repo (first time only)
do: Open PowerShell (or VS Code: Terminal > New Terminal) and run the two lines below. A sign-in window may open: sign in to GitHub. If the folder C:\csc-repo already exists, skip this step.

steps.title: Get the latest online copy
do: Run this before every update so your copy matches GitHub.

steps.title: Copy the new version into the repo
do: Run the line below. Nothing in the repo is deleted. A summary table appears: FAILED must be 0. Exit codes 1 to 7 are normal.
Or copy and paste in File Explorer: open C:\csc-v31, Ctrl+A, Ctrl+C, open C:\csc-repo, Ctrl+V and choose Replace the files in the destination.

steps.title: Open the repo in VS Code and check
do: VS Code: File > Open Folder > C:\csc-repo (choose Yes to trust). Open Terminal > New Terminal: the prompt must end with csc-repo. Run git status.
You should see mostly modified files and a few new ones. If it says hundreds of new files (for example 326), you are in the wrong folder: do NOT commit. Go back to step 2.

steps.title: Add, commit and push
do: Run the three lines one at a time. If a sign-in window opens, sign in and the push continues. If Git asks who you are, see the topic Fix problems after upload.
commands: git commit -m "v31: header and sidebar fixes, new right sidebar"

steps.title: Check the live site
do: Open https://github.com/CSC-VLE-TOOLS-DESK/CSC-VLE-TOOLS and check the latest commit time. Wait 1 to 2 minutes (see the Actions tab). Open your live site and press Ctrl+F5. On a phone, close the tab and open it again.
Check: all header buttons are visible including Theme, both sidebars float with a gap, the right New Tools panel is violet, and 3 or 4 tools open and work.

troubleshooting.fix: You are in the wrong folder. Go to the cloned folder and try again. Commands: cd C:\csc-repo ; git status

troubleshooting.problem: git status shows hundreds of new files (for example 326)
troubleshooting.fix: That folder is not your GitHub repo. It is a plain copy, or VS Code made a new empty repo there (Initialize Repository). Do not commit or push from it. Do not use git push --force. Fix: clone the real repo (topic: Upload to GitHub, step 2) and copy the new version into that clone.

troubleshooting.problem: Git asks: who are you? (first time)
troubleshooting.fix: Run these two lines with your own name and email, then repeat git commit. Commands: git config --global user.name "Your Name" ; git config --global user.email "you@example.com"

troubleshooting.problem: git push says rejected or non-fast-forward
troubleshooting.fix: The online copy has newer changes. Pull first, then push. Commands: git pull --rebase ; git push

troubleshooting.problem: git push asks for a password
troubleshooting.fix: GitHub no longer accepts account passwords. Use the sign-in window that opens (Git Credential Manager) or a Personal Access Token.

troubleshooting.problem: Folder name has # or & and commands fail
troubleshooting.fix: PowerShell cannot read # and & in paths. Use short folders such as C:\csc-v31 and C:\csc-repo, or keep the whole path inside double quotes.

troubleshooting.problem: Site looks old after the push
troubleshooting.fix: Wait 2 minutes, then press Ctrl+F5. Check the Actions tab for a failed build. All pages load files as ?v=31, so old files should not be mixed.

troubleshooting.problem: A tool says it failed to load
troubleshooting.fix: A file was not uploaded. Upload the WHOLE assets folder (js, css, maps, kids) and all .html files, not only some of them. The message names the missing file.
The assets/kids folder was not copied. Run the copy step again.

troubleshooting.problem: I pushed by mistake and want to go back
troubleshooting.fix: Run the first line to see the last commits, then the next two. This undoes the last commit safely and keeps history. Commands: git log --oneline ; git revert HEAD ; git push
